\section{The finite local slope cone}
\begin{lemma}[Local supports imply global PCC inequalities]\label{localglobal}
On the present embedded complex, a continuous function with an ambient
affine local support at every point satisfies every real-endpoint PCC.
For a PA function these supports make \(D_f c\) nonnegative for every
nonnegative balanced cycle \(c\) on a common carrying structure.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Restrict to any segment contained in \(X\) and subtract its endpoint
chord. If the continuous difference has a positive maximum, its maximum
set lies in the open segment and is nonempty and closed. At a maximum
point, a supporting affine function must have zero segment slope:
otherwise it would exceed the maximum on one side. The support then
makes the maximum set open. Connectedness contradicts the zero endpoint
values. Thus the restriction lies below every chord and is convex.
At a PCC center \(x\), the segment to each endpoint \(x_i\) lies in its
incident convex cell. If \(\ell\) is the linear part of a local support
at \(x\), comparison at \(x+t(x_i-x)\) with the segment's endpoint
chord gives \(f(x_i)\geq f(x)+\ell(x_i-x)\). Sum the endpoint
inequalities with their coefficients; the barycenter cancels the
linear terms. For the divisor, a support at a relative interior point
of \(\tau\) agrees with \(f_\tau\) on its tangent space. Subtract that
support in \eqref{raw}; balancing cancels its tangent correction,
and each remaining inward slope is nonnegative. Every application
to a divisor uses PA \(f\) and a common carrying structure.
\end{proof}
Fix a rational point \(p\in\relint(\tau)\) of a carrying structure for a
PA function \(f\). Let \(C_{\sigma/\tau}\) be its tangent cones, including
the common lineality \(N_{\tau,\R}\), and choose finite nonzero rational
generators \(d_1,\ldots,d_m\) of their union. Include a rational basis and
its negatives for lineality. A generator has an incident-cone assignment;
duplicate directions have consistent values because \(f\) is continuous.
On each cone write the affine germ as
\[
 f(p+x)=f(p)+h_p(x).
\]
The continuous homogeneous function \(h_p\) is linear on each cone.
Put \(s_i=h_p(d_i)\), \(U=(d_1\ \cdots\ d_m)\), and
\[
 K(U)=\{\lambda\in\R_{\geq0}^m:U\lambda=0\}.
\]
At a vertex no tangent quotient is taken. This matters: flat two-sided
directions at a singular vertex must remain in the test.

\begin{lemma}[Finite supports]\label{supports}
A continuous finite PA function is PC if and only if, at every face
germ, there is an ambient linear form \(\ell_p\) with
\[
 \ell_p(d_i)\leq s_i\quad(1\leq i\leq m).
\]
Equivalently \(s\cdot\lambda\geq0\) for all \(\lambda\in K(U)\).
These conditions give finitely many rational linear inequalities in the
affine coefficients on any specified finite rational structure. No
simplicial or matroid hypothesis is needed.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For a PC PA function, R230 gives all real-endpoint inequalities (its
continuous completion is itself). Given \(\lambda\in K(U)\), use the
endpoints \(p+\varepsilon d_i\) with common sufficiently small positive
\(\varepsilon\), in their assigned incident cells. Normalize the nonzero
coefficients by \(\sum\lambda_i\). Their center is \(p\), and Jensen gives
\(\sum\lambda_i s_i\geq0\). At a rational \(p\) these endpoints can instead
be chosen rational, so even this local invocation respects the printed
definition directly.

Here is the finite duality argument, without an ungranted Farkas theorem.
The cone
\[
 T=\R_{\geq0}^m+\operatorname{image}(U^\mathsf{T})
\]
is finitely generated: use the coordinate vectors and both signs of a
basis of the image. A finitely generated cone is closed. To see this,
eliminate dependent active columns in a nonnegative representation by
subtracting a signed dependency until one coefficient vanishes. The
remaining columns are independent. On each of finitely many independent
subsets, the inverse column map bounds the coefficients by a constant
times the represented vector's norm. A converging sequence thus has a
subsequence with convergent coefficients on one fixed subset.
If \(s\notin T\), let \(z\) be its nearest point in \(T\). Squared-distance
minimization gives \(\lambda=z-s\) nonnegative on \(T\), with
\(\lambda\cdot z=0\) and
\(\lambda\cdot s=-\|z-s\|^2<0\). Pairing with the coordinate generators
and the image subspace shows \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(U\lambda=0\), a
contradiction. Therefore \(s=b+U^\mathsf{T}\ell_p\) with \(b\geq0\).
The reverse implication follows by pairing this identity with \(K(U)\).

Linearity on each cone extends the generator inequalities to the entire
cone, giving an affine local support at \(p\). The same test at a
rational representative of a face works throughout its relative interior:
the tangent cones and linear parts are unchanged. Thus these are supports
at every real point. Lemma \ref{localglobal} proves every
PCC inequality globally, giving sufficiency without identifying PC with
globally ambient convex functions.

Finally \(K(U)\) is a rational polyhedral cone. Its extremal generators
have minimally dependent positive supports, with one-dimensional kernel
on each support. Such supports have at most
\(\operatorname{rank}(U)+1\) elements. Gaussian elimination gives rational
generators, and there are finitely many subsets to inspect. These
generators span \(K(U)\), by the same finite cone geometry used in R230.
Testing them gives the asserted finite rational inequalities.
\end{proof}

At a vertex \(v\), call a nonzero \(\lambda\in K(U)\) with
\(s\cdot\lambda=0\) a \emph{flat relation}. This means equality in a
nontrivial local PCC, not zero raw mass. It does not depend on the chosen
finite generating list: any local directions can be resolved inside
their assigned cones into generators and conversely generator relations
are local PCCs.

\begin{lemma}[Strict affine floor]\label{floor}
Assume explicitly that the finite PA germ at the vertex is PC, equivalently
$s\cdot\lambda\geq0$ for every $\lambda\in K(U)$. Under this hypothesis,
absence of flat relations is equivalent to existence of an
ambient linear form \(\ell\) with
\[
 h_v(x)-\ell(x)>0\quad
       \text{for every nonzero }x\text{ in the tangent support}.
\]
In that case \(h_v(x)-\ell(x)\geq c\|x\|\) there for some \(c>0\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By B225 the generator cone of the positive balanced star is its span,
so \(K(U)\cap\{\sum\lambda_i=1\}\) is nonempty and compact.
The PC hypothesis makes every relation cost nonnegative. If there is no
flat relation, the minimum of \(s\cdot\lambda\) on this
section is a positive number \(\theta\). Choose \(0<\delta<\theta\).
Then \(s-\delta{\bf1}\) pairs nonnegatively with every element of \(K(U)\).
The separation argument in Lemma \ref{supports} supplies \(\ell\) with
\(s_i-\ell(d_i)\geq\delta\) for every generator.
On each cone a nonzero vector has a nonnegative generator
representation, so its residual is strictly positive. The union of the
finitely many cone sections on the unit sphere is compact; the continuous
residual has positive minimum \(c\). Conversely any such strict residual
pairs positively with every nonzero element of \(K(U)\), excluding a flat
relation. Common lineality is handled by its two opposite generators;
a linear germ on it automatically has a flat relation.
\end{proof}

\section{A necessary local contact condition}
\begin{theorem}[Noncontact forces a flat relation]\label{necessary}
Let \(\gamma\) be a continuous PC reference, \(u\) bounded continuous,
and suppose the actual envelope \(P_\gamma(u)=f\) is finite PA.
If \(f(v)<\gamma(v)+u(v)\) at a vertex of a rational carrying structure
for \(f\), its germ at \(v\) has a flat relation.
This assertion makes no measure or approximation assumption.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The finite envelope is PC: each competitor satisfies Jensen, and taking
the pointwise supremum preserves its inequality. Thus its PA germ has
nonnegative relation costs. Suppose there is no flat relation and apply
the corrected Lemma \ref{floor} with this established hypothesis. In a
sufficiently small ambient ball about \(v\), the space is exactly its
truncated tangent star and \(f(v+x)=f(v)+h_v(x)\). Shrink its radius
\(r>0\) so that the continuous obstacle gap is greater than some
\(\eta>0\) throughout its intersection with \(X\).
For \(0<t<\min(\eta,cr/2)\), define in this ball
\[
 F(v+x)=\max\{f(v+x),\,f(v)+t+\ell(x)\},
\]
and put \(F=f\) outside it. Since \(h_v-\ell\geq c\|x\|\), these
definitions agree on the collar \(r/2<\|x\|<r\). Also
\(0\leq F-f\leq t\), so \(F\) is continuous, lies below the obstacle,
and has the same growth upper bound as \(f\).

At an interior point of the modified region where the affine floor is
active, that floor is a local support. Where \(f\) is active, a local
support of \(f\) from Lemma \ref{supports} remains a support of \(F\).
This also covers tie points, and the collar is unchanged. Lemma
\ref{localglobal} therefore proves \(F\in\PC_q(X)\).
It is an actual competitor in \eqref{env}, with \(F(v)=f(v)+t\),
contradicting maximality.
The inserted floor need not be PA on a rational structure; competitors
in \eqref{env} are not restricted to PA. No operator is assigned to it.
\end{proof}

In particular a finite PA endpoint can have positive noncontact raw mass
only on the boundary of the local slope cone specified by a flat
relation. The theorem is not a claim that every such boundary point
is globally growth-compatible.

\section{Global realization of every compatible PA obstruction}
\begin{theorem}[Exact bounded roof obstruction]\label{obstruction}
Fix a PA PC reference \(\gamma\) in either category \(*=\Z,\R\).
Let \(f\in\PAPC_*(X)\) satisfy \(f-\gamma\in\PA_{*,b}(X)\).
Suppose a vertex \(v\) has a flat relation and genuine raw mass
\(m_v=(D_f^d[X])(v)>0\).
There is an explicitly constructed \(u\in\PA_{*,b}(X)\) such that
\[
 P_\gamma(u)=f\in\PC^{\rm reg}_*(X,\gamma),\qquad
 \int_X(f-(\gamma+u))\MAstar(f)=-R m_v<0
\]
for a positive rational \(R\). In particular the pair cannot have both
all-obstacle endpoint regularity and orthogonality in that category.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Choose a lattice basis and the rational polyhedral norm
\(\rho(x)=\max_j|x_j|\) in its coordinates. Choose rational \(R>0\)
so small that the closed norm ball about \(v\) meets only cells incident
to \(v\), the entire restriction of \(f\) in that ball is its linear
germ on each incident cell, and the ball contains no other vertex of
a chosen common finite carrying structure for \(f,\gamma,[X]\).
These choices are possible by finiteness and the rational vertex \(v\).
Put
\begin{equation}\label{roof}
 B_R(x)=(R-\rho(x-v))_+,\qquad
 u=f-\gamma+B_R,\qquad a=\gamma+u=f+B_R.
\end{equation}
The roof is continuous literal PA on a finite rational hyperplane
subdivision, has integral slopes and rational constants, and vanishes
outside that ball. Thus \(u\) is admissible in the asserted category.
The function \(f\) is a competitor with the actual reference growth.

Write the flat relation as
\(\sum_i\lambda_i d_i=0\), \(\lambda_i\geq0\), and
\(\sum_i\lambda_i h_v(d_i)=0\), discarding zero coefficients.
The rational points
\[
 y_i=v+\frac{R}{\rho(d_i)}d_i
\]
lie in their assigned incident cells and on the roof boundary. Set
\(\beta_i=\lambda_i\rho(d_i)/R\).
Then
\[
 \sum_i\beta_i(y_i-v)=0,\qquad
 \sum_i\beta_i(f(y_i)-f(v))=0.
\]
After normalization this is a printed rational-endpoint PCC at \(v\)
whose endpoint obstacle values equal \(f(y_i)\).
Every competitor \(q\) therefore satisfies \(q(v)\leq f(v)\).

For rational \(x\) with \(0<\rho(x-v)<R\), put
\(y=v+R(x-v)/\rho(x-v)\).
This is a rational point of the same incident cell, on the roof
boundary. The segment from \(v\) to \(y\) is in that cell. Jensen
and the affinity of \(f\) give \(q(x)\leq f(x)\).
Outside the ball the direct obstacle bound already gives \(q\leq f\).
These bounds hold for every rational point and also at \(v\).
For a real point, use successively smaller rational simplices in its
relative rational face containing it. Their rational vertices have
the preceding bound; Jensen and continuity of \(f\) imply \(q(x)\leq f(x)\).
Thus maximality over every printed-PC competitor, including discontinuous
ones, proves \(P_\gamma(u)=f\). Its upper semicontinuous regularization is
the same continuous function.

The measured endpoint is already PA PC and relative; its constant
decreasing regularization is valid. Refinement independence proved
above ensures that new roof-subdivision vertices contribute no new
atoms to \(\MAstar(f)\). The only original atom in the roof support
is \(v\), where the gap is \(-R\). All others have gap zero. Hence
the integral is exactly \(-R m_v\). This proof checks the genuine
operator domain rather than declaring a measure of a continuous hull.
\end{proof}

This theorem needs global compatibility of \(f\), which is the explicitly
stated bounded-difference condition with the \emph{actual} reference.
It does not assert that every abstract bad local germ can be extended
through the remaining complex. Positive growth alone is not used to
replace that condition.

\begin{corollary}[Exact finite-PA-endpoint characterization]\label{scoped}
For a fixed pair and fixed coefficient category, the following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every admissible PA obstacle whose actual envelope belongs to
\(\PAPC_*(X,\gamma)\) has zero raw contact integral.
\item Every \(f\in\PAPC_*(X,\gamma)\), at every vertex of a rational
carrying structure, satisfies: \(m_v(f)>0\) implies absence of a flat
relation.
\end{enumerate}
Here the reference is explicitly PA PC in the chosen category, as required
by Theorem~\ref{obstruction}. The second condition contains neither an
obstacle nor a contact integral.
This is a classification of the finite PA endpoint sector, not original
P05.2 with all regularizable endpoints.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
If (2) holds, the finitely many positive atoms of a PA envelope are
contact points by Theorem \ref{necessary}; every term in its atomic
contact integral vanishes. Conversely a violation of (2) gives the
admissible obstacle and negative integral in Theorem \ref{obstruction},
whose endpoint is in the stated PA category.
\end{proof}

\section{A finite algebraic test with actual global growth}
Fix a finite rational carrying structure \(\Pi\) for \(\gamma,[X]\).
Parameterize affine linear parts and constants of \(f\) on its cells by
coefficients \(z\). Equality of the affine restrictions on shared faces
is a finite rational linear system: test a rational affine basis of each
face. Lemma \ref{supports} at every face gives a finite system
\(Az\geq0\).
For each generator \(r\) of \(\rec(\sigma)\), impose
\begin{equation}\label{growth}
 (f_\sigma-\gamma_\sigma)(r)=0.
\end{equation}
These are exactly bounded difference on the whole complex.
Necessity follows along the rays \(x+tr\); sufficiency follows by
writing a rational polyhedron as a bounded convex hull plus its
finitely generated recession cone. For cells with lineality use both
signs of a basis. If desired, an ambient rational coordinate
hyperplane arrangement splits every cell into pointed cells, leaving
only finitely many vertices and recession rays. Rational finite
generation and this decomposition follow from the elementary
cone-section argument in R230: remove rational lineality, take a
strictly positive rational section of the pointed cone, and obtain
finitely many rational vertices by successive active-constraint
elimination. Applying it to the homogenized cell gives the claimed
vertex-plus-recession decomposition.

On a specified structure, recursive formula \eqref{raw} makes
\(m_v(z)\) a homogeneous degree-\(d\) polynomial in the linear parts,
with the actual top weights and primitive saturated normals as
coefficients. Let \(\kappa_{v,j}\) be the finitely many normalized
extreme relations at \(v\), and \(s_v(z)\) its generator slope vector.
The existence of a bad relative \(\PA_\R\) function \emph{carried by
this structure} is exactly the finite disjunction of systems
\begin{equation}\label{test}
 \text{shared-face equations},\quad Az\geq0,\quad
 \eqref{growth},\quad
 s_v(z)\cdot\kappa_{v,j}=0,\quad m_v(z)>0.
\end{equation}
A flat relation has zero cost on some extreme relation because all
extreme costs are nonnegative. Thus \eqref{test} is an actual
semialgebraic obstruction test, not total mass or orthogonality
renamed. A feasible point gives a global certificate and the roof
obstacle. In the literal category impose integral coordinates of
each tangent linear part in a saturated lattice basis and rational
affine constants as well. A real feasible point is not automatically
a literal one.

Nonsimplicial stars use all their generators and shared-face equations;
no replacement by an ambient strong-convexity cone occurs.
Nonsaturated input directions must first be replaced by the saturated
tangent lattice normals in \eqref{raw}; the relation cone alone does
not encode their intersection indices. Genuine common lineality has
a linear restriction of the germ and hence flat opposite generators.
If a germ is invariant modulo an affine function along nonzero common
lineality, its raw top atom is zero: on the generalized carrying fan
every face contains that lineality, so there are no zero-dimensional
faces. Refinement independence keeps that zero result if artificial
cuts create a vertex.

Testing one structure is not testing all rational refinements, and even
testing all structures only gives Corollary \ref{scoped}'s finite-PA
sector. No bound on the structures needed for arbitrary envelopes is
proved here.

\section{A genuinely coupled two-plane obstruction}\label{coupled-section}
Let $N=\Z^3$, $P_{xz}=\{y=0\}$, $P_{yz}=\{x=0\}$, and
$X=P_{xz}\cup P_{yz}$ with cycle $[X]=[P_{xz}]+[P_{yz}]$.
Both plane lattices are saturated coordinate copies of $\Z^2$; all top
cells of a common rational subdivision have weight one. On a new wall
in one plane the two primitive inward quotient classes are opposites.
On the shared $z$-axis the transverse classes are $\pm e_x,\pm e_y$,
whose sum is zero. Thus this is an actual strictly positive balanced
cycle. Divisor additivity in the cycle, twice, gives
\[
 D_f^2[X]=D_f^2[P_{xz}]+D_f^2[P_{yz}].
\]
This is additivity on a sum of carrying planes; it asserts no product
factorization of $f$ or identification of PC with ambient convexity.

Define the actual ambient convex functions, restricted to $X$,
\[
 \gamma=\max(|x|,|y|,|z|)+|z|,\qquad
 f=\max(|x|,|y|-1,|z|)+|z|.
\]
Each is a maximum of finitely many integral affine forms after resolving
$|z|$, with integer constants and rational carrying walls. Thus both
are continuous literal PA, separately real PA, and PC by ordinary
ambient Jensen for every permitted PCC. Shifting just one entry of a
maximum by minus one gives $-1\leq f-\gamma\leq0$ everywhere.
The reference satisfies $\gamma\geq\rho=\max(|x|,|y|,|z|)$, so its
slope in every nonzero recession direction is strictly positive.
Near zero on the vertical plane $f=2|z|$, giving a flat relation on
$\pm e_y$; on the horizontal plane $f=\max(|x|,|z|)+|z|$.

\subsection{Every first-cycle weight and primitive normal}
Write plane coordinates $(a,b)$ for $(x,z)$ or $(y,z)$, and $s,t\in\{1,-1\}$.
For $h(a,b)=\max(|a|,|b|)+|b|$, all nonzero first-cycle edges are
\[
 \{(sa,0):a\geq0\}\ \text{with weight }2,
 \quad \{r(s,t):r\geq0\}\ \text{with weight }1.
\]
Along the $s$-axis, adjacent gradients are $(s,1),(s,-1)$;
primitive transverse lifts $(0,1),(0,-1)$ give weight two.
On a diagonal the outer and central gradients are $(s,t),(0,2t)$.
The tangent $(s,t)$ and inward lift $(s,0)$ form a saturated basis,
since their determinant is $\pm1$; the opposite lift points centrally.
The difference $(s,-t)$ evaluates to one on $(s,0)$, giving weight one.
Along each nonzero $b$-axis both gradients are $(0,2t)$, so its weight
is zero. There are no further walls: the six affine forms are
$a+b,a-b,-a+b,-a-b,2b,-2b$.
The complete cycle balances at zero, since the two weighted axes cancel
and the four diagonal directions cancel. Its outgoing slopes are one
on the axes and two on the diagonals, so
\[
 (D_h^2[P])(0)=2+2+4\cdot2=12.
\]
There are no other vertices or atoms on this homogeneous plane cycle.

On $P_{yz}$ put $g(a,b)=\max(|a|-1,|b|)+|b|$.
Its complete nonzero first cycle consists of
\begin{enumerate}
\item the central segment $b=0$, $-1\leq a\leq1$, of weight four;
\item the outward axis rays from $(s,0)$ in direction $(s,0)$, of weight two;
\item the two rays from each $(s,0)$ in directions $(s,t)$, each of weight one.
\end{enumerate}
In $|a|<1+|b|$ the function is $2|b|$; outside it is $|a|-1+|b|$.
Across the central segment gradients $(0,2),(0,-2)$ and lifts $\pm e_b$
give four. On each outward axis use $(s,\pm1)$ and the same lifts to
get two. On a diagonal use $(s,t),(0,2t)$ and lifts $\pm(s,0)$ as
above, giving one. Away from the endpoints the artificial lines $a=\pm1$
and the nonzero $b$-axis have identical gradients on both sides, hence
weight zero. The six affine forms are
$a-1+b,a-1-b,-a-1+b,-a-1-b,2b,-2b$;
they show there are no omitted positive walls.

At $p_s=(0,s,0)$, the weighted primitive directions and outgoing slopes are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{direction}&\text{weight}&\text{slope of }f\\\hline
-s e_y&4&0\\
s e_y&2&1\\
s e_y+e_z&1&2\\
s e_y-e_z&1&2
\end{array}
\]
Their weighted sum is $-4s e_y+2s e_y+(s e_y+e_z)+(s e_y-e_z)=0$.
The recursive atom is $4\cdot0+2\cdot1+1\cdot2+1\cdot2=6$.
Subdividing the central segment at zero adds opposite weight-four
$y$ directions of zero slope, hence adds zero atom there.
On the full $X$, the origin also has the horizontal-plane axes and
diagonals just computed; their mass is twelve. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{new-masses}
 \MA(\gamma)=24\delta_0,\qquad
 \MA(f)=12\delta_0+6\delta_{p_+}+6\delta_{p_-}.
\end{equation}
All first-cycle vertex balances have been displayed. At an added vertex
on a straight affine first-cycle edge, equal weights and opposite
outgoing slopes cancel. A new wall inside an affine top cell has
opposite normal contributions and zero first weight. New cells in
old higher-dimensional zero-weight strata inherit zero. These facts,
or the fully converted refinement theorem above, give zero artificial
mass at every vertex of the roof subdivision. No factorial is added.
The gradient polygons have areas six for $h$ at zero and three for
$g$ at each endpoint; twice these areas agrees with the raw calculation.
Polygon area is an independent check, not its operator proof.

\subsection{Unrestricted envelope and both coupling tests}
Set $R=1/4$, $B=(R-\rho)_+$, and $u=f-\gamma+B$.
This obstacle is bounded literal PA on a finite rational arrangement;
$\gamma+u=f+B$ and $f$ is an actual relative PC competitor.
For every printed-PC competitor $q$, including discontinuous ones,
the rational endpoints $(0,\pm R,0)$ have obstacle value zero and
midpoint zero, so $q(0)\leq0=f(0)$. A rational point $w$ with
$0<\rho(w)<R$ lies on the chord from zero to the rational boundary
point $Rw/\rho(w)$. The entire chord is in one incident linearity
cell of $f$; inside this ball $f$ is homogeneous on both planes.
The boundary obstacle equals $f$, so Jensen gives $q(w)\leq f(w)$.
Outside the ball the obstacle itself gives this bound. At an arbitrary
real point take shrinking rational simplices in its minimal rational
face. All their vertices satisfy the rational bound, and the printed
PCC inequality and continuity of $f$ give $q\leq f$ at the center.
No continuity of $q$ is assumed. Therefore $P_\gamma(u)=f$ on all $X$;
its usc regularization is itself. A constant PA regularizing sequence,
or decreasing positive rational additions, works in both categories.
Only the origin has mass in the roof support, so
\begin{equation}\label{new-contact}
 \int_X(f-(\gamma+u))\MA(f)=-R\cdot12=-3.
\end{equation}
Both total masses are twenty-four, which does not establish contact.

The precise excluded decomposition is $f(q,z)=F(q)+H(z)$ on
$X=C\times\R$, $C=\{y=0\}\cup\{x=0\}\subset\R^2$.
At the four horizontal-plane corners $(x,z)=(0,0),(R,0),(0,R),(R,R)$,
the endpoint and reference values are $0,R,2R,2R$.
The mixed difference $f(R,R)-f(R,0)-f(0,R)+f(0,0)=-R$ is nonzero.
The obstacle values there are $R,0,0,0$, with mixed difference $R$.
Thus reference, endpoint, and obstacle all exclude the stated additive
product decomposition. We claim nothing about every possible reparametrized
factorization. Pair-level regularity for other obstacles is not inferred.

\section{Why finite jet presentation does not finish regularization}
Lemma \ref{supports} does give a finite linear feasibility system for
PC affine coefficients on a \emph{specified} structure. Together with
shared-face, obstacle, and growth constraints it gives valid finite
PA trial competitors. It does not prove that this structure carries
the unrestricted envelope, that a finite number of hull iterations
suffices, or that all structures have a uniform approximation theorem.
R230 supplies continuity but none of those conclusions.

There is also a precise coefficient obstruction to treating the
real rational-structure category as closed under taking maxima.
On \(\R\), put \(\alpha=\sqrt2-1\) and
\[
 f_1=|x|,\quad f_2=|x-1|+\alpha,\quad
 t=(1+\alpha)/2=\sqrt2/2.
\]
Both \(f_i\) are real PA on rational structures, PC, and differ
boundedly from \(|x|\). Yet
\[
 \max(f_1,f_2)=\max(x,2t-x)=|x-t|+t
\]
has its unique kink at the irrational point \(t\), so no finite rational
structure on \(\R\) carries it. This is \emph{not} a nonregularizability
example: rational \(t_n\downarrow t\) give literal PA PC functions
\[
 H_n=\max(x,2t_n-x)\downarrow \max(f_1,f_2),\qquad
 \|H_n-\max(f_1,f_2)\|_\infty=2(t_n-t).
\]
Thus a finite maximum argument needs its own rational-structure and
approximation audit; the failure of PA closure alone proves no
endpoint regularization failure.

\section{Global realization of finite local jets for rational references}\label{jet-section}
Here $\gamma$ is rational affine on a finite rational structure, PC, and
positive at infinity. The target coefficient category is the explicitly
real scalar extension, even when $\gamma$ is literal. We do not assert
that the following scaling/gluing is literal.

\begin{theorem}[Actual-reference jet realization]\label{jet-realization}
At a rational point $v\in X$, let $h$ be a continuous homogeneous PA PC
function on a finite rational refinement of the tangent star of $X$ at
$v$, with $h(0)=0$. If all affine linear parts of $h$ are rational,
then there is a global rational-affine relative real PA PC function
$G$ whose germ at $v$ is $C+t+\delta h$, for positive rational
$\delta,t$ and rational $C$. In particular flat relations are preserved
and the raw atom is $\delta^d m_0(h)$.
If a real-coefficient such jet has a flat relation and positive raw
atom, some rational-coefficient jet on the same specified structure
has these properties and hence is globally realized with the actual
reference.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The space equals its truncated tangent star in a sufficiently small
rational norm ball about $v$; insert $v$ and the chosen local rational
fan subdivision. The finite linear pieces of $h$ give
$|h(x)|\leq L\rho(x)$ on this tangent support for some $L$.
Choose rational $\varepsilon>0$ so the ambient $\varepsilon\rho(x-v)$
has recession slopes strictly smaller than those of $\gamma$.
The coercive linear lower bound proved in Lemma~\ref{test-dc} permits
this choice. Take rational $C>\gamma(v)$ and put
\[
 \Psi(x)=\max\{\gamma(x),C+\varepsilon\rho(x-v)\}.
\]
Both entries have local supports. The maximum is rational-affine PA
PC, agrees with $C+\varepsilon\rho$ near $v$, and differs boundedly
from $\gamma$, because its second entry is below $\gamma$ outside a
compact set. Choose a rational star radius $r>0$, and rational
$\delta>0$ with $\delta L\leq\varepsilon/2$. Choose rational
$0<t<\varepsilon r/4$. Inside $\rho(x-v)<r$ define
\[
 G(x)=\max\{\Psi(x),C+t+\delta h(x-v)\},
\]
and set $G=\Psi$ outside. On the collar $r/2\leq\rho<r$,
$C+\varepsilon\rho\geq C+t+\delta h$, so these definitions agree.
Near $v$, $\Psi=C+\varepsilon\rho$ and the raised jet is strictly
active for sufficiently small $\rho$; hence the germ is precisely
$C+t+\delta h$. Local supports of $h$ follow from the finite support
criterion; supports of an active entry support the maximum, also at
ties. The collar glues without a new defect. The global support lemma
therefore gives every PCC inequality. All coefficients and all norm-ball,
fan and equality walls are rational, so the structure is finite rational.
The modification of $\Psi$ has compact support and is bounded. Thus
$G-\gamma$ is genuinely bounded with the actual prescribed growth.
Raw recursion in the local star is unchanged by the constant and scales
by $\delta^d$; flat relation costs scale by $\delta$.

For a real-coefficient bad jet, the finitely many shared-face and PC
conditions on its fixed fan are rational linear conditions. Some rational
extreme relation has zero cost: decompose its flat relation into extreme
relations and use nonnegative costs. Adjoin that rational linear
zero-cost equation. Rational points are dense in this feasible rational
polyhedron, including at its boundary, by solving the active rational
equalities as equalities and approximating in their rational affine
solution space (inactive inequalities remain strict). The raw mass is
a continuous degree-$d$ polynomial in the slopes, with the actual
fixed top weights, so its strict positivity persists under a sufficiently
close such rational approximation. This gives the claimed rational bad
jet, and the first construction applies. No arbitrary local germ is
asserted literal-realizable.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Structural finite-PA contact criterion]\label{local-finite}
For rational-affine positive-growth $\gamma$, real-category contact for
all bounded real PA obstacles whose actual envelopes are finite relative
PA is equivalent to the following condition on the weighted rational
geometry of $X$: at every rational point and every finite rational
refinement of its tangent star, each PC homogeneous PA jet with a flat
relation has zero raw top atom. This condition contains no actual
reference or global extension premise; its raw recursion uses the
saturated tangent lattices and actual weights.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
If the condition holds, apply it to the germ of any positive-mass
finite PA envelope vertex. There can be no flat relation there, so the
corrected noncontact theorem forces contact. Conversely a bad local jet
has a globally realized relative real PA function by
Theorem~\ref{jet-realization}. The exact roof theorem gives an admissible
real PA obstacle with that endpoint and strictly negative contact integral.
Its coefficient and regularizable antecedents are already checked.
\end{proof}

The universal quantifier over rational star refinements is essential.
Each fixed fan has the finite circuit/mass test already proved, but no
bound on the necessary refinements follows. This is now a geometric
criterion for the finite PA endpoint sector and this rational-reference
scope. It still does not classify all regularizable non-PA endpoints or
establish regularity for every continuous obstacle.

\section{A genuine extension on the regularizable domain}\label{extension-section}
This section goes beyond finite endpoints. Its reference hypothesis is
\emph{rational affine coefficients on a finite rational structure}, not
arbitrary real coefficients. Literal references satisfy it. We retain
finite pure positively balanced embedded $X$, real finite raw intersections,
and positive growth of the actual reference $\gamma$.
We do not import BMPS Theorem 4.13 or Proposition 4.16: their needed
conclusions in this scope are reconstructed below. In particular no
operator is assigned just because an envelope is continuous.

\begin{lemma}[Raw degree and integration by parts]\label{raw-ibp}
All mixed finite PA PC functions $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ with bounded difference
from $\gamma$ have total raw mass $M=\deg(\gamma)$.
For bounded finite PA $b,c$ and any intermediate balanced one-cycle $Z$,
\[
 \int bD_c Z=\int cD_b Z.
\]
Both statements allow real coefficients and zero intermediate weights.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Refine so every function is affine on every edge of $Z$; cut lines at
rational points if necessary. On an unbounded edge a bounded affine
function has zero slope. For a bounded edge $[v,w]$ of primitive length
$L_e$, its contribution to $\int bD_c Z$ is
\[
 \frac{Z(e)}{L_e}(b(v)-b(w))(c(w)-c(v)),
\]
which is symmetric in $b,c$. Sum the finite list of edges. Also
$\deg(D_b Z)=0$: bounded-edge outgoing slopes cancel, and unbounded
slopes vanish. Replace each mixed factor $a_i$ by $\gamma$ one at a
time; the difference is $D_{a_i-\gamma}$ of the balanced one-cycle
formed by the other $d-1$ factors, so it has degree zero. Positivity
was proved by local supports and balanced preservation above.
For later use, the bounded-difference identity is
\begin{equation}\label{relative-ibp}
 \int(\gamma-q)\MA(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_d)
 =\int(\gamma-a_1)\MA(q,a_2,\ldots,a_d)
  +\int(a_1-q)\MA(\gamma,a_2,\ldots,a_d).
\end{equation}
It follows by applying the bounded $b,c$ identity to
$b=\gamma-q$, $c=a_1-\gamma$, then expanding linearly.
All measures in this displayed formula are finite raw measures.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Test functions as differences of relative PC functions]\label{test-dc}
Let $\psi$ be a compactly supported ambient continuous PA function with
rational affine coefficients on a finite rational complex in $N_\R$.
There are rational $\varepsilon>0$ and rational-affine relative PA PC
functions $\theta_0,\theta_1$ on $X$ such that
$\theta_1-\theta_0=\varepsilon\psi|_X$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose the finite rational hyperplane arrangement containing every wall
of $\psi$, with integral normal forms $L_j$ and rational constants.
Across each wall the two gradients of $\psi$ differ by a scalar multiple
of its normal. There are finitely many such multiples. For a sufficiently
large rational $K>0$, $H=K\sum_j|L_j|$ and $H+\psi$ are ambient convex:
on a generic segment their slopes increase at every wall, since the
bend $2K$ dominates every negative bend of $\psi$; limiting generic
segments prove the same for all segments. Both are rational affine on
this arrangement.

Positive growth and the finite vertex-plus-recession decompositions give
$\gamma(x)\geq a\rho(x)-b$ on $X$ for some $a>0,b$.
Indeed the ratio of its positive recession linear part to $\rho$ has
a positive minimum on the finite unit recession sections; the finitely
many bounded hulls change only the constant. Take rational
$\varepsilon>0$ so small that $\varepsilon H$ has recession slopes
strictly below those of $\gamma$, using its finite Lipschitz constant.
Choose rational $C$ so $C+\varepsilon H>\gamma$ on a neighborhood of
$\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap X$. Define
\[
 \theta_0=\max(\gamma,C+\varepsilon H),\qquad
 \theta_1=\theta_0+\varepsilon\psi.
\]
The first maximum has local supports and hence is PC. Near the support
of $\psi$, the second function is $C+\varepsilon(H+\psi)$; outside
that support it equals $\theta_0$. These open descriptions cover $X$
and give local supports everywhere, including the collar where
$\psi=0$. Both functions differ boundedly from $\gamma$: the added
maximum is inactive outside a compact set. All their affine coefficients
are rational, so all new equality walls are rational and both functions
are real PA on finite rational structures. They need not be literal PA;
only the already verified finite real raw operator is used for them.
For an irrational-coefficient reference these new maximum walls need
not be rational, which is why that category is excluded from this lemma.
\end{proof}

The restrictions of these compact ambient rational PA tests are uniformly
dense in $C_c(X)$, allowing supports in a fixed larger compact set.
Here is a direct construction. For a nonnegative $g\in C_c(X)$, fix a
small uniform-continuity scale $\delta$ for $g$ on the closed finite
polyhedral support $X$. Such a scale exists: outside a compact
neighborhood $g=0$, and inside it a finite compactness cover gives the
scale. Choose an integer $L$ larger than $2\|g\|_\infty/\delta$ and a
sufficiently fine finite rational net of the compact set where $g$ may
be nonzero. Approximate its sampled values by nonnegative rational
$a_j$ and set
\[
 G(x)=\max_j(a_j-L\rho(x-v_j))_+.
\]
For $\rho(x-v_j)\geq\delta$ the corresponding bump vanishes;
for smaller distances it exceeds $g(x)$ by at most the chosen
uniform-continuity and sampled-value errors. A net finer than the
error divided by $L$ gives the reverse inequality. Thus the error
can be arbitrarily small. This is compactly supported ambient rational
PA with rational equality walls. Apply the construction separately to
$g_+$ and $g_-$ for a signed function. No false density in all
$C_b(X)$ is asserted.

\begin{theorem}[Failure of global weak uniform continuity]\label{uniform-failure}
On the balanced unit-weight line with actual reference $\gamma(x)=|x|$,
the finite raw operator is not globally uniformly continuous for the weak
uniformity generated by $C_b(\R)$, even on literal relative PA PC functions.
On the real relative PA domain it is not globally uniformly continuous
for the bounded-Lipschitz metric either.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For integers $n\geq1$, put $A_n=|x-2n|$ and
$B_n=|x-2n-1/(8n)|$. A carrying structure has the rational vertices
$0,2n,2n+1/(8n)$ and their complementary edges. The affine formulas
have slopes $\pm1$ and rational constants. Both functions are ambient
convex, so satisfy every printed rational-endpoint PCC. Their differences
from the actual $|x|$ are bounded, with norms $2n$ and $2n+1/(8n)$;
their two recession slopes are one. They are actual literal PA PC
endpoints with constant decreasing regularizations. Primitive outgoing
normals on the line are $\pm1$. Away from each kink the opposite slopes
cancel, while the two outgoing slopes at the kink are both one. Thus
\[
 \MA(A_n)=2\delta_{2n},\quad \MA(B_n)=2\delta_{2n+1/(8n)},\quad
 \|A_n-B_n\|_\infty=1/(8n).
\]
For the single fixed test $\psi(x)=\sin(\pi x^2)$, which is bounded
and continuous, the absolute evaluation difference is
$2\cos(\pi/(64n^2))\to2$. This violates one fixed defining entourage
of the weak $C_b$ uniformity.

For even $n$ let $a_j=4j$ for even $j$, $a_j=4j+1$ for odd $j$,
and let $b_j$ make the opposite choices, $0\leq j<n$. Set
$A_n=n^{-1}\sum_j|x-a_j|$, $B_n=n^{-1}\sum_j|x-b_j|$.
Each sum is a convex function on the rational line subdivision by these
finitely many integer points, with rational slopes and constants. Its
outer slopes are $-1,1$; hence it has bounded difference from $|x|$
and the prescribed positive recession growth. It belongs to real PA on
finite rational carrying geometry and is already regularizable there.
This need not be literal PA. Raw linearity in the actual one-cycle gives
\[
 \MA(A_n)=\frac2n\sum_j\delta_{a_j},\qquad
 \MA(B_n)=\frac2n\sum_j\delta_{b_j}.
\]
For a pair $j=2k,2k+1$, its unnormalized difference is
\[
 |x-8k|-|x-8k-1|+|x-8k-5|-|x-8k-4|.
\]
It vanishes outside $[8k,8k+5]$, rises linearly from zero to two
on $[8k,8k+1]$, equals two on $[8k+1,8k+4]$, and falls to zero
on $[8k+4,8k+5]$. These pair intervals are disjoint. Therefore
$0\leq A_n-B_n\leq2/n$ and the uniform distance is exactly $2/n$.
Let $\eta$ be the continuous eight-periodic linear interpolation through
$(0,1/4),(1,-1/4),(4,-1/4),(5,1/4),(8,1/4)$.
It has sup norm $1/4$ and Lipschitz constant $1/2$; it belongs even
to the convention $\|\eta\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(\eta)\leq1$.
Its values at every $a_j,b_j$ are $1/4,-1/4$, respectively, so the
raw measure evaluation difference is exactly one for every even $n$.

The relative norm of a sum of these shifted absolute values against
$|x|$ is exactly its average shift: the triangle inequality gives the
upper bound, attained on $x\leq0$. Both averages equal
$2(n-1)+1/2=2n-3/2$. They grow without a common fixed bound. These
families are not uniformly convergent to one relative function. The
failure concerns global uniform continuity, not the convergence result
proved next. It is a material restriction of the old guarantee.
\end{proof}

We specify all output notions. The vague topology and uniformity are
generated by finite lists of evaluations $\nu\mapsto\int g\,d\nu$,
$g\in C_c(X)$. The weak $C_b$ topology and uniformity use finite lists
with $g\in C_b(X)$. Fix a Euclidean metric on $X$ and define
\[
 d_{\rm BL}(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{\|g\|_\infty\leq1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(g)\leq1}
              \left|\int g\,d(\mu-\nu)\right|.
\]
All measures below have the same finite raw mass $M$. The domain metric
on tuples is $d_\infty(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)=\sum_i\|f_i-g_i\|_\infty$.
For each category $*$, let $\mathcal D_*(\gamma)$ be the uniform closure
of the actual relative $\PAPC_*$ functions in continuous functions of
bounded difference from the same actual reference. No other continuous
PC function is added by definition.

\begin{lemma}[Positive-functional representation]\label{radon-lemma}
On the closed finite polyhedral metric space $X$, every positive linear
functional $L$ on $C_c(X)$ satisfying $|L(g)|\leq M\|g\|_\infty$ is
integration against a unique finite positive Radon measure of mass at
most $M$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For open $O$, define
$\alpha(O)=\sup\{L(h):h\in C_c(X),0\leq h\leq1,
\operatorname{supp}h\subset O\}$.
It is at most $M$. If $O\subset\bigcup_iO_i$, the compact support of
any such $h$ has a finite subcover. A continuous partition on a neighborhood
of that support, with compact supports subordinate to the selected opens,
exists by taking finitely many small relatively compact balls, continuous
distance cutoffs, and dividing their sum where it is positive. It splits
$h$ into nonnegative functions $h_i\leq1$ supported in $O_i$.
Hence $\alpha(O)\leq\sum_i\alpha(O_i)$. For disjoint opens finite
sums of admissible tests are again at most one; taking suprema gives
$\alpha(\bigcup_iO_i)\geq\sum_i\alpha(O_i)$, first for finite sums
and then for all finite partial sums.

Set $\mu^*(A)=\inf_{O\supset A}\alpha(O)$ over open supersets.
Choosing open supersets within arbitrary summable errors proves countable
subadditivity, so this is an outer measure. If two sets have positive
distance, their disjoint distance neighborhoods, intersected with any
open superset of their union, give
$\mu^*(A\cup B)=\mu^*(A)+\mu^*(B)$.
Here is the Borel measurability step in detail. For a closed $E$ and
arbitrary $A$, put $A_j=A\cap\{\operatorname{dist}(x,E)\geq2^{-j}\}$.
Separated-set additivity gives
$\mu^*(A)\geq\mu^*(A\cap E)+\mu^*(A_j)$.
The shells of $A\setminus E$ between successive positive dyadic distances
have finite total outer mass: any finite collection of even-index shells
is pairwise separated and has summed outer mass at most $M$, and the
same is true for odd-index shells. Consequently the sums of all shell
masses converge and their tails tend to zero. Countable subadditivity
then gives
$\mu^*(A\setminus E)\leq\lim_j\mu^*(A_j)$.
This is the Caratheodory inequality for $E$; its reverse is subadditivity.
Thus all closed, hence all Borel, sets are measurable. The restriction
$\mu$ is a countably additive finite measure, since the outer-measure
identity for measurable disjoint sets and continuity of finite partial
sums give countable additivity.

For open $O$ one has $\mu(O)=\alpha(O)$ directly by monotonicity in
open supersets. If $h$ is an admissible test and $K=\operatorname{supp}h$,
then $L(h)\leq\alpha(W)$ for every open $W\supset K$, whence
$L(h)\leq\mu(K)$. This proves inner compact regularity on opens;
outer regularity is the definition of $\mu^*$. For a Borel set, choose
an open superset of arbitrarily small excess measure and apply inner
regularity to its complement in a sufficiently large compact set.
Since $\alpha(X)$ is approximated by compactly supported tests, such
compact sets exhaust its mass. This proves inner regularity on all
Borel sets as well.

For $g\in C_c(X)$ nonnegative, let $R=\|g\|_\infty$ and $\delta=R/n$.
Tests $h_k$ supported in $\{g>k\delta\}$ satisfy
$\delta\sum_{k=1}^n h_k\leq g$; maximizing each of their functional
values gives the lower bound
$L(g)\geq\delta\sum_{k=1}^n\mu\{g>k\delta\}$.
For the upper bound choose a compact cutoff equal to one on
$\operatorname{supp}g$, and for each $k\geq1$ a test equal to one
on the compact set $\{g\geq k\delta\}$ and supported in
$\{g>(k-1)\delta\}$. Their sum times $\delta$, together with
$\delta$ times the first cutoff, majorizes $g$.
Thus
$L(g)\leq\delta M+\delta\sum_{k=1}^n\mu\{g>(k-1)\delta\}$.
The two sums differ by at most $\delta M$ and also bracket the integral
of $g$ by elementary pointwise step bounds. Letting $n\to\infty$
proves $L(g)=\int g\,d\mu$. Signed functions follow by their positive
and negative parts. Conversely, compact cutoffs and inner regularity
recover open-set masses from these integrals, proving uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Raw completion with the exact continuity scopes]\label{raw-extension}
Fix finite pure positively balanced embedded rational $X$ and the actual
rational-affine PA PC positive-growth reference $\gamma$ of this section.
For $*=\Z,\R$, the finite raw mixed operator extends uniquely to
$\mathcal D_*(\gamma)^d$. Its outputs are positive finite Radon measures
of raw mass $M=\deg(\gamma)$; the extension is symmetric, local, and
agrees with the finite raw recursion. Arbitrary uniformly convergent PA
approximants give the same limit against every $C_b$ test.

The extension is continuous from the uniform domain topology into the
weak $C_b$ topology (for sequences and nets). It is globally uniformly
continuous into the vague $C_c$-test uniformity. For \emph{each fixed}
$0\leq C<\infty$, on
\[
 \mathcal F_{*,C}=\{(f_1,\ldots,f_d)\in\mathcal D_*(\gamma)^d:
                   \max_i\|f_i-\gamma\|_\infty\leq C\},
\]
it is uniformly continuous into the weak $C_b$ uniformity and in
$d_{\rm BL}$. These last two assertions have no entire-domain
uniform-continuity conclusion. If $M=0$, all outputs are zero and
all the asserted continuity properties are immediate.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Assume $M>0$. For a compact ambient rational PA test $\psi$, the preceding
DC lemma gives $\theta_1-\theta_0=\varepsilon\psi$ with actual relative
real PA PC functions and fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For two relative finite
PA PC tuples, telescope one factor at a time. The other factors form
positive balanced one-cycles $Z_i$, so bounded edge integration by parts
and raw positivity give
\begin{equation}\label{test-estimate}
 \left|\int\psi\bigl(\MA(\mathbf a)-\MA(\mathbf b)\bigr)\right|
 \leq \frac{2M}{\varepsilon}\sum_i\|a_i-b_i\|_\infty.
\end{equation}
Indeed $D_\psi Z_i=(D_{\theta_1}Z_i-D_{\theta_0}Z_i)/\varepsilon$
has total variation at most $2M/\varepsilon$. This constant depends on
the test and actual reference, \emph{not} on relative sizes of $\mathbf a$
or $\mathbf b$. Auxiliary real functions are legitimate even when the
approximating tuples are literal, because their finite real raw recursion
has already been established; no new literal endpoint is inferred.

For a uniform-Cauchy tuple of approximants, the integrals in
\eqref{test-estimate} are Cauchy. Uniform density of compact rational PA
tests in $C_c(X)$, with supports controlled as proved above, and the
common mass $M$ show that every $C_c$ integral is Cauchy: replacing a test
within $\eta$ costs at most $2M\eta$ in a difference. The limits define
a positive linear functional bounded by $M\|g\|_\infty$.
Lemma~\ref{radon-lemma} gives its unique positive Radon measure $\mu$.

We prove mass and tightness without changing the actual reference.
Choose a fixed rational $c\geq0$ so $H=\gamma+c\geq0$ on $X$.
This is possible by the coercive lower bound; $H$ is a proper height.
The raw reference measure remains $\MA(\gamma)$ by constant invariance.
Put $J=\int H\MA(\gamma)<\infty$, and for integers $j\geq1$ set
\[
 q_j=\max(\gamma+c-j,0)-c=\max(\gamma-j,-c).
\]
These are relative rational-affine PA PC functions on finite rational
structures; $\gamma-q_j=\min(H,j)$.
For a finite tuple with $\max_i\|a_i-\gamma\|_\infty\leq D$,
apply the previously proved relative IBP identity with $q=q_j$.
Split $a_1-q_j=(a_1-\gamma)+(\gamma-q_j)$.
The first two terms have absolute values at most $DM$ each, by positive
mixed measures of mass $M$. The remaining term replaces $a_1$ by
$\gamma$. Repeat through all $d$ factors, obtaining
\begin{equation}\label{moment}
 \int\min(H,j)\MA(\mathbf a)\leq2dDM+J=:K_D.
\end{equation}
Monotone convergence over $j$ gives the same bound for $\int H$.
Consequently $\MA(\mathbf a)\{H>T\}\leq K_D/T$.

A particular uniformly convergent family of approximants has one finite
$D$. Choose continuous compact cutoffs $\chi_T$ equal to one on
$\{H\leq T\}$, with $0\leq\chi_T\leq1$.
Vague convergence gives $\int\chi_T\,d\mu\geq M-K_D/T$ and the
representation gives $\mu(X)\leq M$. Hence $\mu(X)=M$.
Nonnegative compact tests majorized by $H$ pass to the limit with the

Truncating a fixed $g\in C_b(X)$ by $\chi_T$ costs at most

Vague convergence of the truncated test, then $T\to\infty$, proves

Comparing any two approximating tuples by \eqref{test-estimate} proves
sequence independence. Passing that estimate along approximants for
any two completed tuples gives \emph{the same} compact-test estimate
on the completion. If $\mathbf f\in\mathcal F_{*,C}$, choose approximants

\eqref{moment} and then taking its supremum gives the exact bound
\begin{equation}\label{completed-moment}
 \int H\,d\MA(\mathbf f)\leq K_C=2dCM+J,
 \qquad \MA(\mathbf f)\{H>T\}\leq K_C/T
       \quad(\mathbf f\in\mathcal F_{*,C}).
\end{equation}
Thus the common constant applies to \emph{all} completed tuples in
this fixed-$C$ family, not just a selected sequence. Using approximants
within one would also give the valid weaker constant $K_{C+1}$.

For a fixed $g\in C_c(X)$ approximate it uniformly within $\eta$ by
one compact rational PA test $\psi$. For \emph{all} completed tuples,
\[
 |\langle g,\MA(\mathbf f)-\MA(\mathbf h)\rangle|
 \leq2M\eta+L_\psi d_\infty(\mathbf f,\mathbf h),\qquad

First choose $\eta$, then the input distance. Finite lists use the

Now fix $C$ once and for all and $g\in C_b(X)$. With the preceding

At one completed tuple $\mathbf f$, its input ball of radius one is
contained in $\mathcal F_{*,C_f}$ where
$C_f=1+\max_i\|f_i-\gamma\|_\infty$.
The last assertion proves ordinary continuity at $\mathbf f$ into

For the bounded-Lipschitz metric, use the same fixed $C$ and cutoff

To prove this, cover $K$ by finitely many balls of radius $r$ and

Symmetry follows from finite raw symmetry. For locality, let two limiting

\section{A non-PA regularizable coupled endpoint with an explicit measure}\label{nonpa-section}
Keep the actual literal reference and balanced $X$ from
Section~\ref{coupled-section}. Define the even convex function
\[
 a(y)=\begin{cases}
 0,&|y|\leq1,\\
 (|y|-1)^2/2,&1\leq|y|\leq2,\\
 |y|-3/2,&|y|\geq2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad F=\max(|x|,a(y),|z|)+|z|\quad\hbox{on }X.
\]
The derivative of $a$ increases from zero to one on the positive side,
and the negative side is its reflection; it is convex and continuous.
Thus $F$ is a restriction of an ambient convex continuous function,
$-3/2\leq F-\gamma\leq0$, and its horizontal restriction is still $h$.
Its vertical restriction at $z=0$, $1<y<2$, is a quadratic, so it is

For $n\geq0$ put $N=2^n$, $h_N=1/N$, and let $a_N$ interpolate the

\[
 0\leq a_N-a\leq1/(8N^2).
\]

from its chord: the error is $(t-t_j)(t_{j+1}-t)/2$.
Therefore
\[
 F_N=\max(|x|,a_N(y),|z|)+|z|\downarrow F,\qquad
 \|F_N-F\|_\infty=1/(8N^2).
\]
All slopes and constants of $a_N,F_N$ are rational. Equality walls of
their maxima are rational, so they are real PA on finite rational
complexes. They are actual relative PC functions with the displayed
common growth bound. Thus $F\in\PC^{\rm reg}_{\R}(X,\gamma)$ and

Here are all raw atoms of these approximants, without substituting

At the initial point $(1,0)$ the central weight-four edge, outward

Their balance is $-4e_y+2e_y+(1,k_0)+(1,-k_0)=0$ after weighting;
the outgoing slopes give $0+2k_0+2k_0+2k_0$.

To verify their entire first-cycle neighborhood, the $z=0$ edges have

\section{The literal antecedent on noncompact finite spaces}\label{literal-section}
The following is a reconstruction of the dossier's noncompact literal
obstruction, not an additional caller grant or a new claim of priority.
It clarifies the literal branch of the original task before any measure
is assigned to an endpoint.

\begin{theorem}[Noncompact literal obstruction]\label{literal-general}
Let $X\subset N_\R$ be a noncompact finite rational polyhedral space,
and let $\gamma$ be literal PA PC and positive at infinity.
Then some bounded literal PA obstacle has an envelope with a positive
uniform distance from every literal PA PC function. Thus the pair
fails the all-PA-obstacle regularity antecedent. Balancing is not needed.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Choose a rational point $x$ in a noncompact connected component and
rational $C>\gamma(x)$. Put $\phi=\max(\gamma,C)$ and
$D=\phi-\gamma$. These are literal PA; $\phi$ is PC by Jensen for
maxima, and $D\geq0$ has compact support by positive growth.
Take a finite common rational subdivision carrying them and split
cells by a coordinate arrangement so that every cell is pointed.
Every unbounded cell has $D=0$: an affine bounded function has zero
slope on its recession rays, and its value along any such ray must
vanish eventually because $D$ has compact support. Thus a positive
cell of $D$ is bounded.

The selected component is path connected through finitely many
polyhedral cells. Since $D(x)>0$ but $D=0$ far out, some bounded
positive-dimensional cell $\sigma$ has nonzero linear part $k$ of $D$.
Choose a primitive $w\in N_\sigma$ with $k(w)\ne0$ and a rational
segment $I=x_0+[0,L]w$ inside its relative interior.
Let $N>|k(w)|$ be an integer and set
\[
 f=\gamma+D/N=(1-1/N)\gamma+\phi/N.
\]
It is continuous real PA on this rational structure, PC by Jensen,
and differs boundedly from $\gamma$. We now produce a \emph{literal}
obstacle, not merely the fractional difference $D/N$.

For every vertex $v$ of this finite structure choose one sufficiently
large integer $M$ so that
\[
 C_v(y)=D(v)/N+M\rho(y-v)\geq D(y)/N\quad(y\in X).
\]
Such a common $M$ exists. On cells incident to $v$ the affine linear
parts bound the difference by a finite slope constant times $\rho$.
The finite union of nonincident closed cells has positive distance
from $v$, while $D$ is globally bounded, so their ratios are bounded
as well. Take the maximum over the finitely many vertices and round
up to an integer. Set
\[
 u_N=\min\left(D,\min_v C_v\right).
\]
All entries have integral slopes and rational constants; minima and
norm walls give a finite rational literal structure. Moreover
$D/N\leq u_N\leq D$, $u_N(v)=D(v)/N$ at every vertex, and $u_N=0$
on every unbounded cell. Thus $f\leq\gamma+u_N$ and $f$ is a competitor.

Every other competitor $q$ has $q(v)\leq f(v)$ at the vertices.
For a rational point $y$ of a pointed cell, write its vertex-plus-recession
representation $y=\sum_v\alpha_vv+\sum_r\beta_rr$ with rational
nonnegative coefficients and $\sum_v\alpha_v=1$; rational Gaussian
elimination of the feasible rational system gives such coefficients.
Choose $v_0$ with $\alpha_{v_0}>0$ and large rational $T$ with
$\sum\beta_r/T<\alpha_{v_0}$. Replace the indicated portions of the
$v_0$ coefficient by weights $\beta_r/T$ at the endpoints $v_0+Tr$.
This is a PCC in that same cell. Those far endpoints are in its
unbounded part, where obstacle and $f$ agree; their values are
$f(v_0)+T f_\sigma(r)$. Jensen therefore gives exactly $q(y)\leq f(y)$.
If there are no recession terms this is just the vertex combination.
The vertex-plus-recession decomposition follows by homogenizing the
rational cell and using the finite rational generating-cone argument
already supplied by R230; pointedness ensures vertices exist.
Shrinking rational simplices give the same bound at real points.
Therefore the unrestricted envelope is $f$.

On $I$ its slope is $q_0=\gamma_\sigma(w)+k(w)/N\notin\Z$.
For a literal PA PC function $\psi$, slopes on this contained primitive
segment are nondecreasing integers: ordinary segment convexity follows
from continuity and rational endpoint Jensen. At the midpoint its
right-hand slope is either at most $\lfloor q_0\rfloor$ or at least
$\lceil q_0\rceil$. Compare respectively the left or right half
increments with the affine target. If uniform error is $\eta$, then
\[
 \eta\geq\frac L4\operatorname{dist}(q_0,\Z)>0.
\]
This excludes literal uniform regularization. No literal extended
Monge--Ampere measure is assigned to this envelope.
\end{proof}

In the fixed globally embedded BMPS category, B225's positive-balanced

\section{A further sector: every continuous obstacle on a finite graph}\label{graph-sector}
The new progress beyond the continuity repair is in dimension one. Here
we allow the \emph{actual} $\gamma\in\PA_\R(X)\cap\PC_q(X)$ to have
arbitrary real, including irrational, affine coefficients, on a finite
\emph{rational} carrying graph. The graph is globally embedded, finite,
pure, and has actual positive real edge weights $w_e$ satisfying lattice
balancing. Its vertices and edge lengths in primitive coordinates are
rational. The conclusion is for \emph{all} $u\in C_b(X)$, not just finite
PA obstacles. Abstract compact chart spaces are outside this theorem.

For each vertex $v$ let $u_{e/v}$ be the primitive outgoing direction and
\[
 K_v=\{\lambda\geq0:\sum_{e\ni v}\lambda_eu_{e/v}=0\}.
\]
The actual weight vector $w_v$ is strictly positive and lies in $K_v$.
We may insert a rational bivalent vertex on a line without vertices;
its cone is one ray, and this does not change the operator or contact.

\begin{lemma}[Continuous graph slopes and supports]\label{graph-slopes}
A continuous printed-PC function $f$ is ordinarily convex on every edge.
Its outgoing one-sided derivatives $d_{v,e}$ are finite at every vertex,
and satisfy $d_v\cdot\lambda\geq0$ for every $\lambda\in K_v$.
Conversely, continuous edgewise convex functions with these finite
vertex derivatives and inequalities satisfy every PCC. They have
ambient affine local supports at every point.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Contained-edge Jensen inequalities pass from rational to real endpoints
by continuity; thus they give ordinary convexity. For rational $t>0$
small enough on every germ, the endpoints $v+t u_{e/v}$ are rational.
The weighted relation $w_v$ gives
$\sum_e w_e(f(v+tu_{e/v})-f(v))/t\geq0$.
Each quotient is nondecreasing as $t$ increases, and is bounded above
near zero by its finite quotient at one fixed small radius. Its limit
therefore lies in $[-\infty,\infty)$; none can be $-\infty$, because
all $w_e>0$ and all other terms have fixed finite upper bounds.
This proves finite derivatives. Applying the same endpoint construction
to any $\lambda\in K_v$ and passing $t\downarrow0$ gives the inequality.
The coefficients can be real; the actual endpoints remain rational.

Conversely the finite duality proof in Lemma~\ref{supports}, applied
to the matrix of primitive directions, gives an ambient $\ell_v$ with
$\ell_v(u_{e/v})\leq d_{v,e}$. Convexity on each germ gives
$f(v+tu_{e/v})\geq f(v)+t d_{v,e}$, hence this is a local support
at $v$. At an edge interior point the left and right convex derivatives
are finite; any slope between them is a supporting affine function
on its line and can be extended ambiently. Thus there are supports at
every point, and Lemma~\ref{localglobal} proves all real-endpoint PCC
inequalities. No PA or operator premise was used in this lemma.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[All-continuous real graph regularization]\label{graph-density}
For the actual real PA reference $\gamma$ positive at infinity, every
$f\in C(X)\cap\PC_q(X)$ with bounded difference from $\gamma$ is a
uniform decreasing limit of relative $\PAPC_\R$ functions on finite
rational carrying structures. In particular every unrestricted envelope
$P_\gamma(u)$, $u\in C_b(X)$, lies in this real regularizable domain.
The statement asserts no literal integral-slope density.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Refine the original graph so $\gamma$ is affine on its edges. Use the
primitive coordinate on each edge. On an unbounded end, for $t\geq T_e$
write $\gamma(t)=g_et+c_e$, $g_e>0$, with a fixed rational $T_e$.
Convexity of $f$ and bounded relative difference force its limiting
slope to be $g_e$. Indeed secant slopes at infinity tend to $g_e$,
and monotonicity of convex derivatives identifies their limit with
that secant limit. Therefore $r_e(t)=f(t)-g_et$ is convex,
nonincreasing, and bounded. It has a finite limit $l_e$.
For any $\eta>0$ choose rational $S_e\geq T_e$ so
$r_e(S_e)-l_e<\eta$. Replace the tail of $f$ by
$f(S_e)+g_e(t-S_e)$, which majorizes $f$ and differs from it by at
most $\eta$. Its slope $g_e$ is at least every preceding chord slope.

On every bounded edge, and every initial segment $[0,S_e]$ of an end,
choose a sufficiently fine finite mesh of rational coordinates including
all vertices, and interpolate the \emph{actual real values} of $f$.
Convex chords majorize $f$, are uniformly close by uniform continuity
on these finitely many compact intervals, and have nondecreasing slopes.
At an original vertex the new outgoing first chord slope is at least
$d_{v,e}$, on both ends of every bounded edge. Since all relation
coefficients are nonnegative, every vertex relation cost remains
nonnegative. At newly inserted bivalent vertices, monotone edge slopes
give exactly the same condition. Lemma~\ref{graph-slopes} proves PC.
Shared vertex values are unchanged, so the resulting function is
continuous. Its affine slopes and constants are real, and all mesh
positions are rational; hence it is actual $\PA_\R$ on a finite
rational structure. Each tail has the \emph{actual} $g_e$ slope,
so bounded difference from $\gamma$ is preserved globally.
The errors can be made arbitrarily small on the whole graph, including
all ends. This construction never takes a finite PA maximum with the
irrational reference, and has introduced no irrational carrying wall.

Extract errors $\leq2^{-n}$ and add $4\cdot2^{-n}$ as in
Theorem~\ref{raw-extension}. The resulting relative real PA PC sequence
is strictly decreasing and converges uniformly. Finally R230 applies
to this finite positive balanced embedded graph and the actual
continuous PC reference: for any $u\in C_b$ its unrestricted envelope
is continuous, PC, and satisfies $|P_\gamma(u)-\gamma|\leq\|u\|_\infty$.
The just-proved approximation applies to that actual endpoint. This is
an operator-domain antecedent, not merely CONT PC membership.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Genuine graph raw completion for all real coefficients]\label{graph-operator}
On the domain in Theorem~\ref{graph-density}, the sequence-independent
uniform completion of the primitive one-dimensional raw operator is
\[
 \Delta f=\sum_v\left(\sum_{e\ni v}w_ed_{v,e}\right)\delta_v
          +\sum_e w_e\,d(f'_+)\big|_{\operatorname{relint}e}.
\]
The second terms are pushforwards in the primitive edge coordinate;
there is no Euclidean arclength or additional factorial. The output is
positive, local, finite, and has mass $M=\sum_{\text{ends }e}w_eg_e
=\deg(\gamma)$. Every uniform PA approximating family converges against
all $C_b$ tests, and agrees with literal raw recursion when restricted
to its actual literal completion domain.

For each fixed $C<\infty$, all these completed real outputs with
$\|f-\gamma\|_\infty\leq C$ satisfy the common tail bound
\[
 \Delta f(X\setminus K_R)\leq\frac{2C}{R}\sum_{\text{ends }e}w_e,
 \quad R>0,
\]
where $K_R$ contains all bounded edges and the end portions
$0\leq t\leq T_e+R$. In addition, choose fixed rational $c$ with
$H=\gamma+c\geq0$ and let $J=\int H\,d\Delta\gamma$. Every completed
function in that same fixed-$C$ family has
$\int H\,d\Delta f\leq2CM+J$. The map is continuous for weak $C_b$, globally
uniformly continuous for vague $C_c$, and uniformly continuous for
weak $C_b$ and $d_{\rm BL}$ on every such \emph{fixed-$C$} family.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For a convex edge function, $f'_+$ is nondecreasing and right continuous.
Right continuity follows directly from the convex secant inequalities:
the right limit of $f'_+$ at $t$ is bounded above by every secant from
$t$ to $t+h$, and taking $h\downarrow0$ gives $f'_+(t)$ itself.
On a compact interval construct positive test functionals from sums
$\sum_i g(\xi_i)(f'_+(t_{i+1})-f'_+(t_i))$.
Two such sums on a common refinement differ by at most the oscillation
of $g$ at their mesh scale times the finite derivative variation.
They therefore converge for continuous tests, are positive and linear,
and the positive-functional lemma constructs their Radon measure.
Continuous level cutoffs and right continuity identify its interval
values, including any endpoint jump. Its Stieltjes measure is determined by
$d(f'_+)((a,b])=f'_+(b)-f'_+(a)$. This determines a positive measure:
on finite intervals, step approximations of the monotone derivative
construct its distribution measure by the same open-set or monotone
interval construction as in Lemma~\ref{radon-lemma}. Countable additivity
follows by continuity of the monotone distribution from the right and
finite interval subdivision; equivalently positive integration functionals
on compact continuous tests and that lemma give the identical interval
values. The finite endpoint derivatives in Lemma~\ref{graph-slopes}
and the limiting end slope $g_e$ give finite edge mass.
Vertex coefficients are nonnegative by the actual relation $w_v$.
On a bounded edge of primitive length $L$, its interior mass is
$w_e(f'_-(L)-f'_+(0))$; its two endpoint contributions to the vertex
sum are $w_ef'_+(0)$ and $-w_ef'_-(L)$. They cancel exactly.
On an unbounded end the interior mass is $w_e(g_e-d_{v,e})$;
adding its vertex contribution leaves $w_eg_e$. Summing the finite
edge list proves the mass identity. Applied to PA functions this is
exactly the actual primitive-normal recursion, including zero artificial
vertices, and proves $M=\deg(\gamma)$.

For a compact rational ambient PA test $\psi|_X$, edgewise Stieltjes
integration by parts gives
\begin{equation}\label{graph-ibp}
 \int\psi\,d\Delta f=\int f\,d\Delta\psi.
\end{equation}
Here $\Delta\psi$ is the signed finite primitive raw divisor of the
compact test against $[X]$. To justify the identity, on each interval
where $\psi$ is affine, integrate its constant derivative against the
increments of $f$, and integrate $\psi$ against the increments of the
monotone $f'_+$. Telescoping interval partitions gives
$\int\psi\,d f'_+=[\psi f']-\int\psi'f'\,dt$.
The latter ordinary integral equals the corresponding affine-test slope
times the endpoint increment of $f$: convex functions with finite
endpoint slopes are Lipschitz on the interval and their increments are
the integrals of their monotone derivatives, as follows by upper and
lower secant Riemann sums. The derivative jumps of $\psi$ supply
$\int f\,d\psi'$. At vertices the boundary terms cancel against the
explicit weighted vertex derivatives on both sides of
\eqref{graph-ibp}. Unbounded edges have no outer boundary term because
the test vanishes there. Constants and continuity cancel the remaining
tangent values. This proves the identity without assuming PA for $f$.

It follows that
$|\langle\psi,\Delta f-\Delta h\rangle|
\leq\|\Delta\psi\|_{\rm TV}\|f-h\|_\infty$.
Uniform density of compact rational PA tests, with controlled supports,
and mass $M$ give convergence for every $C_c$ test and sequence
independence. Locality follows directly from the displayed derivative
formula, or from localized tests in \eqref{graph-ibp}.
For $\|f-\gamma\|_\infty\leq C$, convexity implies
\[
 f'_+(T_e+R)\geq\frac{f(T_e+R)-f(T_e)}R
                         \geq g_e-2C/R.
\]
The end measure beyond that point is
$w_e(g_e-f'_+(T_e+R))\leq2Cw_e/R$.
This proves the asserted common bound for \emph{every} completed function
in the family. A uniformly convergent approximation to a fixed relative
function has a common finite $C$, so compact cutoff truncation upgrades
its vague convergence to every $C_b$ test. At one input use a radius-one
uniform neighborhood with $C_f=1+\|f-\gamma\|_\infty$ to get ordinary
weak-$C_b$ continuity. The compact-test estimate gives global vague
uniform continuity. For each fixed $C$, the common end-tail bound and
finite compact-test approximation give weak-$C_b$ uniform continuity;
the finite mesh and value-quantization net of BL restrictions on $K_R$
from Theorem~\ref{raw-extension} gives BL uniform continuity with
that same fixed $C$. If $M=0$, positivity gives the zero output and
all claims are immediate.
For completeness the moment bound holds for all these outputs even with
irrational coefficients of the actual reference. The continuous convex
$q_j=\max(\gamma-j,-c)$ is boundedly relative to $\gamma$.
It is not asserted to have rational carrying walls; Theorem~\ref{graph-density}
places it in the actual real completion by rational chords. Its measures
and those chord approximants have already been proved to converge for
all $C_b$ tests. For finite relative PA $a$, apply the finite bounded
edge IBP identity to actual PA approximants of $q_j$ and pass to the
limit, using the bounded differences as tests. This gives
\[
 \int(\gamma-q_j)\Delta a
 =\int(\gamma-a)\Delta q_j+\int(a-q_j)\Delta\gamma.
\]
The first term and the part $a-\gamma$ of the second have absolute
value at most $CM$ each; the remaining term is
$\int\min(H,j)\Delta\gamma\leq J$.
Approximate any completed $f$ with relative bounds $C+o(1)$ and use
all-$C_b$ convergence on the bounded test $\min(H,j)$ to obtain
$\int\min(H,j)\Delta f\leq2CM+J$. Monotone convergence proves
the stated common moment bound for every completed function in the
fixed-$C$ family. This application has an actual operator antecedent
for $q_j$ before any measure is used.
There is no arbitrary-relative-bound weak
uniform guarantee; the line counterexamples still apply.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[All-continuous graph contact classification]\label{graph-contact}
For the finite globally embedded positive balanced rational graph and
actual positive-growth $\gamma\in\PA_\R\cap\PC_q$ of this section,
the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every $u\in C_b(X)$ has a real-regularizable actual envelope and
$\int(P_\gamma(u)-\gamma-u)\Delta P_\gamma(u)=0$.
\item $K_v=\R_{\geq0}w_v$ at every vertex.
\end{enumerate}
If the second condition fails, an actual bounded real PA obstacle already
has a finite relative real PA PC envelope with a strictly negative
contact integral, even for irrational coefficients of the actual reference.
This is a one-dimensional sector theorem, not the full original P05.2.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
All actual envelopes have their real-domain antecedent and genuine
operator by Theorems~\ref{graph-density}--\ref{graph-operator} and R230.
Let $f=P_\gamma(u)$ and suppose the local cones have one ray.
At a noncontact vertex with positive atom, its derivative vector $d_v$
has $d_v\cdot w_v>0$, hence strictly positive cost on every nonzero
relation. The corrected strict-floor separation argument applies to
this finite derivative vector: it gives $\ell$ and $c>0$ with
$d_{v,e}t-\ell(tu_{e/v})\geq c\|tu_{e/v}\|$ on every germ.
Edge convexity gives the same lower bound for
$f(v+tu)-f(v)-\ell(tu)$. On a small star with positive continuous
obstacle gap, raise $f$ to
$\max(f,f(v)+b+\ell(x-v))$ with $b$ less than the gap and the strict
collar margin; outside leave it unchanged. Supports of $f$ exist by
Lemma~\ref{graph-slopes}, and supports of active entries persist at
ties. The collar makes the localized function continuous and PC by
Lemma~\ref{localglobal}. It preserves actual growth and raises $f(v)$,
contradicting the unrestricted envelope. Thus every noncontact vertex
has zero atom. No finite PA germ for $f$ was assumed here.

At an interior noncontact point choose a sufficiently small closed
edge interval $[a,b]$ in the positive-gap set, with oscillation of $f$
less than the gap there. Replacing $f$ on that interval by its chord
raises it by less than that gap. The incoming derivative at $a$ is
at most the secant slope and the outgoing derivative at $b$ is at
least it, so the glued edge remains convex. All original vertex
derivatives are untouched, hence supports and PCC inequalities remain
valid. If $f$ were not affine there, this would be a competitor raising
an interior point. Consequently $f$ is locally affine throughout the
open noncontact portion of every edge, and its curvature measure
vanishes there. Together with the vertex conclusion, the positive
measure is supported on the closed contact set. Its total mass is
finite and the gap is bounded continuous, giving the exact zero integral.

For necessity suppose $\dim K_v>1$. Since $w_v$ is strictly positive,
$K_v$ has dimension $\dim\ker U_v$. Choose an extreme ray $\kappa$
of this rational cone. It omits some edge coordinate $e_0$:
otherwise an independent kernel vector would permit small two-sided
perturbations of its strictly positive coefficients, contradicting
extremality. The ray can be chosen rational by the finite circuit proof.
Set $s_{e_0}=1$ and all other $s_e=0$. This homogeneous rational
edgewise affine germ $h$ is nonnegative, has the zero local support,
and is PC; $s\cdot\kappa=0$ while its actual raw mass is
$s\cdot w_v=w_{e_0}>0$. Real positive weights are retained exactly.

We realize this germ with the \emph{actual irrational-coefficient}
reference, using graph interpolation rather than irrational PA maximum
closure. Coercivity gives $\gamma\geq a\rho-b_0$. Choose rational
$\varepsilon>0$ smaller than $a$, and rational $C>\gamma(v)$.
The continuous PC function
$\Psi=\max(\gamma,C+\varepsilon\rho(x-v))$ equals its second entry
near $v$ and equals $\gamma$ outside a compact set. It is \emph{not}
asserted to belong to rational-geometry PA. Choose a rational star
radius $r$, rational $\delta>0$ with $\delta|h|\leq\varepsilon\rho/2$,
and rational $0<t<\varepsilon r/4$.
Inside the star set $G=\max(\Psi,C+t+\delta h)$ and outside set $G=\Psi$.
The same strict collar and local-support argument as in the rational
jet theorem gives a continuous PC global $G$, boundedly relative to
the actual $\gamma$, with germ $C+t+\delta h$.

Now apply the \emph{proved graph} chord construction to $G$, choosing
its first rational sample on every germ at $v$ inside that unchanged
linear germ. The first chord is exactly the germ; subsequent meshes,
other vertex slopes, and tail slopes have the properties proved in
Theorem~\ref{graph-density}. This produces an actual relative
$F\in\PAPC_\R$ on finite rational geometry with the same germ at $v$,
flat relation $\kappa$, and raw mass $\delta w_{e_0}>0$.
It need not have rational coefficients elsewhere; these are allowed
real coefficients on rational carrying cells. Both $F$ and the actual
$\gamma$ are now on finite rational structures, so $F-\gamma$ is
bounded real PA. The exact rational roof theorem applies in that real
category, producing $u=F-\gamma+(R-\rho(x-v))_+$ with actual
unrestricted envelope $F$ and contact $-R\delta w_{e_0}<0$.
All endpoint and operator antecedents are verified. The intermediate
continuous maximum received no operator from its continuity; it was
replaced by an actual PA function before the roof calculation.

Subdivision adds only bivalent stars with a single relation ray, so the
condition is intrinsic to this carrying graph. The proof uses global
embedded coercivity and does not transfer the necessity construction
to abstract compact charts. It also proves no higher-dimensional
approximation or non-PA contact criterion.
\end{proof}
